title: Choose the visual world for Before The Heat
question: The roll assigned the Rod & Colour Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each card shows the Murrini editor with the new rod-slice canvas.

options.label: Rod & Colour Chart
options.lineage: Glass makers' printed rod and colour catalogues: coded chips, COE stamps, tabular specs
options.thesis: Every colour is a coded chip and every design ends up as a catalogue entry you can build.
options.viewport: Cobalt catalogue band with tabs. Tools grouped as Single cane / Bundles on the left. The rod slice is drawn at true scale on white with a mm ring scale and gather → pulled Ø readouts. On the right, the casing stack as chart rows and a grid of named, coded colour chips. A plan strip runs along the bottom.
options.risk: A white catalogue page can read clinical, like a spec sheet, and it breaks the current dark habit; chips need borders to hold contrast on white.

raised.raise: All codes, mm, ratios and COE values sit in one tabular-figure column grammar, at chart density.
The slice owns the field: chrome recedes and the cross-section is the one object at full weight.
Claim and proof: every plan step carries the crop of the cross-section it builds.

options.label: Held to the Light
options.lineage: Holding a murrine slice up to a window or lightbox to read its colour
options.thesis: Glass is judged by transmitted light, so the slice sits on a lit bed and colour reads the way it will in the finished piece.
options.viewport: A graphite frame shell with tabs. The centre is a luminous bed where the slice is lit from behind, casing rings translucent, and opaque colours visibly block light. Panels sit in the frame's dark margin.
options.risk: This is the direction most glass-themed runs land on (glow). The translucency rendering must be physically honest or it breaks accuracy, and the dark frame drifts back toward the current look.

options.label: Slide Rack on the Light Bed
options.lineage: Pocket timetable read as tinted glass slides on a lit goldenrod bed
options.thesis: Each build step is a tinted glass slide in one raked rack. Rank comes from weight and reversal, never size.
options.viewport: A goldenrod bed with the slice on one opaque ivory pane. The build steps run as a raked lateral rack of slides with a tick rail for position.
options.case: The strongest audience identification of the hand: tinted glass on a light table is the user's own world. It loses on clarity because the rake and the single type size fight a dense editor.
options.risk: Raked containers and one type size make the dense Murrini controls harder to scan; this could become a costume.

options.label: Construction Grid
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel gridded specimens: forms built cell by cell on a visible armature
options.thesis: The slice is built on a visible mm construction grid, so canes snap to cells and the grid is the scale.
options.viewport: A white sheet with faint blue mm gridlines across the work area. The slice sits on the grid with snapped canes, and monumental grid-built diameter numerals show gather and pull.
options.case: Clearest product mechanism: true scale and snapping make every placement a dimension. Audience identification is weaker because it reads as engineering before glass.
options.risk: Graph-paper precision can feel like CAD, not craft; the grid competes with dense patterns.

options.label: Shop Wayfinding
options.lineage: Airport overhead sign bands: one decision per band, monumental gate numbers
options.thesis: The plan is a chain of decision points: the next step is signed huge and the rest of the route waits.
options.viewport: A yellow sign band across the top names the next step. The slice sits below with the step's canes lit, and the route of remaining steps runs as a band row.
options.case: Best clarity for the phone checklist in the shop. Glassblowers don't identify with airports, and yellow collides with cadmium-yellow colorant data.
options.risk: Yellow as UI chrome competes with yellow glass; the editor inherits checklist energy it doesn't need.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: Ikeda datamatics: black/white barcode fields, dense monospace
options.thesis: The design as a black-and-white data field.
options.viewport: A black field of bars with the slice as a sampled column.
options.case: It loses both axes: colour is this product's content, and a no-colour world erases it.
options.kept: Tabular density: every number set in one column grammar.
options.risk: Removes colour from a colour product.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.lineage: Saville's Factory Records sleeves: fac numbers, colour codes for words
options.thesis: Every design gets a catalogue number and is named in colour code.
options.viewport: A black field, one plot, a fac number.
options.case: It loses both axes: coding names away hurts learners, and the rod chart already carries real codes.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.lineage: Neutral-scale software marketing with one accent
options.thesis: A neutral scale and one accent, every claim paired with proof.
options.viewport: Neutral panels with a single accent.
options.case: It loses both axes: this is the generic look the critique flagged.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark pro creative tool, like the canvas apps people already use, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A left tool rail with icons, a centre canvas, and a right inspector with collapsible sections.
canonCard.risk: It reads like every design tool, which is close to the current look.
